# Skilled Nursing News: operators' MA contract management

- Citation: Skilled Nursing News, "Inside Nursing Homes' Contract Management for Overcoming Medicare Advantage Burdens", 2026-09. https://skillednursingnews.com/2026/09/inside-nursing-homes-contract-management-for-overcoming-medicare-advantage-burdens/
- Year: 2026
- Tier: 3 (trade news; operators quoted)
- Who: Elizabeth McLaren, SVP Revenue Cycle Reimbursement and HCBS, Covenant Living Communities and Services; Danielle Dang, VP Clinical Reimbursement, EF Senior Care.
- Key points: contract decisions weigh "retrospective denials, the number of times staff must touch a claim before it is paid, payment timelines, prior and continued-stay authorization requirements, portal functionality, and even the amount of staff time spent communicating with the payer". Covenant walked away from contracts where MA reimbursement "approaches Medicaid levels but requires substantially more administrative work". Covenant manages about 120 MA contracts; its Traditional Medicare share of short-stay admissions fell from about 58% (FY2021) to about 42%. Tactics: plan-level margin analysis, carve-out negotiation, centralized prior auth, dashboards on approvals, denials and payment speed.
- Limits: two operators; read via a summarizing fetch.
